recognize_zh: 箭頭所指的晚期紅血球母細胞，核旁細胞質內有數顆小而圓、深紫色、類似 Howell-Jolly 小體的核碎片；旁邊還有核分裂象與大型空泡狀細胞，屬於骨髓造血不良（MDS）的紅系異形變化。
features: Late erythroblasts with round nuclei and clumped chromatin (arrows)
Multiple small, round, dense, dark-purple Howell-Jolly body-like inclusions in erythroblast cytoplasm adjacent to the nucleus
Other erythroblasts with fine peripheral dot-like inclusions at the cell margin
A mitotic figure (left) and immature cells with open chromatin in the field
Occasional large vacuolated cell and granulocytic precursors in the background
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows erythroid precursors with multiple small, round, densely basophilic cytoplasmic inclusions resembling Howell-Jolly bodies (arrows), indicative of nuclear fragmentation/karyorrhexis. A mitotic figure and scattered immature myeloid cells are also present. These nuclear debris-type inclusions within erythroblasts represent dyserythropoiesis. Findings are consistent with dyserythropoietic change as seen in myelodysplastic neoplasm, to be correlated with blast count, cytogenetics and exclusion of nutritional or drug-related causes.

ddx.vs: Megaloblastic erythroblasts show nuclear-cytoplasmic asynchrony with open sieve-like chromatin and giant metamyelocytes, and correct with vitamin replacement.
Pappenheimer bodies are smaller, clustered granules that stain with Prussian blue, whereas Howell-Jolly body-like inclusions are larger DNA remnants.
Drug-induced dyserythropoiesis may look identical and requires clinical history and resolution after withdrawal.
CDA presents in young patients with isolated erythroid dysplasia such as internuclear bridging or binucleation, without cytopenias of other lineages or clonal markers.
